delegated_by: maintainer (issue #116 owner), instructing that Jev do the review
note: Not a human review. Labels were compared with five blind Jev readings and re-read once by the model that wrote the held-out labels. Nothing here replaces a person confirming them.

auditors.name: claude
auditors.role: second read of all 150 labels and adjudication of contested cases; also wrote the 100 held-out labels, so it is not independent of them

result.finding: No label was found to be wrong. One labelling-convention inconsistency was found: short-form named artifacts are treated as the whole output for some nouns (tagline, slogan, blurb, bio, welcome message, email body) and as a part for others (headline, title, subject line, greeting, code comment). Both are context-dependent; consumers should abstain when the scope is ambiguous, which `partial` >= 0.40 does.
result.explanation: 141 criteria agree with their label in all five runs and 9 do not. The 15 contested criteria are those 9 plus 6 that agreed in every run but have ambiguous scope, so the two counts overlap and must not be added.

jev_as_verifier.outcome: negative result; not used to decide anything
jev_as_verifier.v1: Asked whether a proposed label was a faithful summary. Accepted both questions for 69 of 150 true labels and 3 of 150 deliberately wrong controls; it rejected every null label because 'cannot be checked' is not a summary.
jev_as_verifier.v2: Asked whether the criterion requires the proposed constraint. Accepted 80 of 95 true labels but also 13 of 95 wrong controls, and rejected trivially correct labels such as 'exactly 6 words' for 'The slogan is exactly 6 words' because it cannot tell whether 'the slogan' is the whole output, which is the scope question under audit.

policy.why_partial_is_0.40: Among null-labelled criteria that could yield a check and are blocked only by `partial`, the lowest `partial` seen in any run is 0.49; run-to-run range is up to 0.15 and typically 0.02. 0.40 leaves about 0.09 of clearance. Fitting the cutoff exactly is unstable: leave-one-criterion-out picks 0.45 in 149 folds and 0.50 in one, and that fold yields a wrong check.
caveats: The cutoff was chosen after seeing the held-out split, so held-out numbers are optimistic.
No untouched labelled set exists; more labels would be needed to tighten the wrong-rate bound.
The 150 criteria over-represent checkable and hard cases; real prevalence is unknown.

null_labelled_cases_that_could_yield_a_c.note: Null-labelled criteria for which Jev's kind, operator and bound would produce a check in at least one run if no abstention rule fired. Criteria that cannot produce a check (for example held-084, which reads sentence_count with operator none, or held-085, which reads other) are not confident-wrong risks whatever their `partial` is.
